rules.title: S.2983 - An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. Reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to Senate Ways and Means; not law, and the page does not show operative terms.
rules.key_value: pending bill prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.effective_date_note: Not enacted; referred to Senate Ways and Means 3/12/2026.

rules.title: H.5222 - An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending House bill aimed at preventing algorithmic rent fixing. Reported favorably 3/12/2026 and referred to House Ways and Means; not law, and operative terms are not shown on the page.
rules.key_value: pending bill; no operative text shown
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.effective_date_note: Not enacted; referred to House Ways and Means 3/12/2026.

rules.title: State bar on local rent control
rules.requirement: Cities and towns in Massachusetts may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. A narrow exception allows only voluntary, municipally compensated regulation for owners of 10 or more units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.key_value: state bar on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: Effective date not stated in the documents.
rules.exemptions: Voluntary regulation after six months, owners of 10+ units, fair market rent not exceeding $400, municipal compensation from general funds.
rules.interaction: Bars local rent control in cities such as Boston and Cambridge.

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 - statewide rent increase cap (removed from ballot by SJC)
rules.requirement: The proposed ballot initiative would have repealed the ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5% for most units. The SJC ruled in June 2026 it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: Lesser of CPI or 5% (never took effect)
rules.quoted_span: annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, educational/religious/nonprofit facilities.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment of rent under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant keeps the tenancy by paying all rent due with interest and costs by the answer day; delays by government in delivering payments require a hearing continuance of at least 7 days.
rules.key_value: 14 days' written notice to quit for nonpayment
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.effective_date_note: No date stated in the document.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenancies under a written lease where rent is unpaid.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: Either party must give three months' written notice to end a tenancy at will (or the rent interval or 30 days, whichever is longer, if rent is paid at intervals under three months). For nonpayment, 14 days' notice to quit applies, with a 10-day right to cure for tenants without a similar notice in the prior 12 months.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days for nonpayment with 10-day cure right
rules.quoted_span: Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party
rules.effective_date_note: No date stated in the document.
rules.penalty: If the notice omits the required cure-right statement, the tenant's time to pay is extended to the answer day.

unverifiable_exemptions: applies only to tenancies at will, not fixed-term leases

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for reporting code violations, enforcing housing laws, or tenants' union activity. Damages are 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages if greater, plus fees; a termination notice (other than nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change within six months is presumed a reprisal.
rules.quoted_span: shall be liable for damages which shall not be less than one month's rent or more than three month's rent, or the actual damages sustained by the tenant, whichever is greater, and the costs of the suit, including a reasonable attorney's fee
rules.effective_date_note: No date stated in the document.
rules.penalty: Damages of 1 to 3 months' rent or actual damages if greater, plus costs and attorney's fees

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment: required state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment of rent must come with the state form documenting repayment agreements and giving rental assistance and legal information, stating that the notice is not an eviction. Courts will not accept a nonpayment summary process filing without proof the form was delivered.
rules.key_value: State form required with nonpayment notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section
rules.effective_date_note: No date stated in the document.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law
rules.requirement: A landlord may collect a security deposit of no more than the first month's rent, held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts bank account with a receipt and condition statement. It must be returned, less itemized permitted deductions, within 30 days after the tenancy ends, with 5% annual interest or the bank rate if lower.
rules.key_value: Max = first month's rent; separate interest-bearing account; return within 30 days
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date of the cap not stated; Aug. 1, 2025 amendment (2025, c. 9) only added agents and fee-in-lieu authority.
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit; three times the deposit plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Limits on upfront payments at tenancy start (no landlord application fee)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord or agent can require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Application and screening fees are not on the list.
rules.key_value: First, last, security deposit, lock/key only
rules.quoted_span: no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.effective_date_note: Text extending the limit to the lessor's agents effective 2025-08-01 (2025, c. 9); the underlying limit predates this (secondary source says since the 1970s).
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational tenancies of 100 days or less.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.review_note: Application-fee reading comes from secondary source D054; statute text lists permitted charges only.

rules.title: Broker fees payable only by the party who engaged the broker
rules.requirement: A licensed broker may contract solely with either the tenant or the landlord, and any fee must be paid only by the party who engaged the broker. A landlord who hires the broker cannot shift the fee to the tenant.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by party who hired the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Text as amended by 2025, c. 9, § 43 effective August 1, 2025 (see § 136).

rules.title: Fair housing law: ban on discrimination based on public assistance / housing subsidy
rules.requirement: Anyone furnishing rental accommodations may not discriminate against an applicant or tenant because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a requirement of such a program.
rules.key_value: ban on discrimination based on public assistance / housing subsidy status
rules.quoted_span: to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date for subsection 10.

no_rule_findings.finding: No Massachusetts statute on algorithmic rent setting is enacted; bills S.2983 and H.5222 are pending.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: Bills banning the practice in the rental market are also working their way through the Massachusetts state House and Senate

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts has no rent cap; state law bars local rent control and the proposed statewide cap was blocked from the ballot.
